text.p: Following is the full text of a statement released by Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA .
PRESS RELEASE
TRACTEBEL SHOWS CONTINUED GROWTH AND ANNOUNCES MERGER WITH POWERFIN - 3 POWERFIN SHARES FOR 1 TRACTEBEL SHARE

TRACTEBEL, the Belgian industrial services and public utilities multinational, today announced its imminent merger with POWERFIN, its 63%-owned subsidiary. This move represents a further significant step in the group's internationalisation and the streamlining of its organisation. It confirms TRACTEBEL's and Belgium's place among the leaders in the world electricity and natural gas markets .

The proposal will be submitted to the EGMs of the respective companies, and the merger itself will be effected by an exchange of one new TRACTEBEL share for three POWERFIN shares. The fairness of the exchange, both for TRACTEBEL shareholders and for POWERFIN shareholders and from the financial point of view, has been confirmed without reservation by SBC WARBURG, a division of SWISS BANK CORPORATION, and by KREDIETBANK SECURITIES and PETERCAM SECURITIES, in their capacity as investment banks.
TRACTEBEL has also announced continued growth in 1996, with net consolidated profits rising to BEF 12.1 billion, 6.7% up on 1995.
Results summary

In 1996, the TRACTEBEL group showed continued growth and expanded its internationalisation programme. The group now has installed generating capacity of more than 22,500 MW, including 9,600 MW outside Belgium.

The group's technical installations and waste management activities grew strongly in 1996. The main contributors to this improvement in the results during 1996 were the companies in the FABRICOM group, which, taking account of those companies consolidated by the equity method, achieved a turnover of BEF 63 billion, 55% of it earned abroad.

Commenting on the 1996 results, Baron Philippe Bodson, CEO of TRACTEBEL and Chairman of its General Management Committee, stated:

Since the end of 1989, TRACTEBEL has been pursuing an ambitious strategy of international expansion in its core activities. Given the rapid globalisation of markets, it is essential for the group to adapt its organisation to match. The merger with POWERFIN represents an essential step in this direction, giving TRACTEBEL the means to achieve its ambition, and follows on from the regrouping of the Belgian electricity companies and the establishment of ELECTRABEL in 1990.

The utilities sector is expanding strongly all over the world. Even in mature economies, opportunities are springing up everywhere with the liberalisation of e electricity and gas markets. The TRACTEBEL group is now a player to be reckoned with in this world market. It has all the technical, financial and human resources necessary to push through a strategy that will create value for all its shareholders.
This international expansion would not be possible without a secure home base in Belgium, as our 1996 results amply demonstrate.
Seconding the remarks of Baron Philippe Bodson, Emmanuel van Innis, member of the General Management Committee and Chief Financial Officer, said:

In financial terms, the merger between TRACTEBEL and POWERFIN represents a logical rationalisation of the group's organisation, strengthening its financial resources and increasing its visibility on the international stage. The merger will also significantly increase the liquidity of the shares on the stock exchange, to the benefit of the shareholders of both companies.

The Board has appointed Mr. Antoon Dieusaert as a director, and appointed Messrs. De Keersmaeker and Dieusaert to the Restricted Committee. At the Extraordinary General Meeting on 28 May 1997, the Board intends to make a proposal reconstituting the Restricted Committee as a Strategic Committee.
More detailed information is attached.

TRACTEBEL SHOWS CONTINUED GROWTH AND ANNOUNCES MERGER WITH POWERFIN 1. Results for Financial Year 1996
Table omitted.
2. Investments

The TRACTEBEL group is the main private investor in Belgium. In 1996, investments by the group came to around BEF 64 billion, including 48 % outside the Belgian electricity and gas sector. 3. TRACTEBEL-POWERFIN merger
The boards of TRACTEBEL and POWERFIN have announced their agreement on the terms of a proposed merger between the two companies, with retrospective effect from 1 January 1997.
3.1 Objectives The proposed merger meets several objectives:

- to strengthen the group' s organisation at international level, by concentrating its efforts on a single investment vehicle with increased financial resources. The success of the TRACTEBEL group's policy of internationalisation must not be allowed to obscure the difficulties frequently encountered by POWERFIN in qualifying for certain projects, especially in the gas sector;
- to simplify the structure of the group, in order to raise its profile on the international markets and reduce certain operating costs;
- to improve the liquidity of TRACTEBEL shares, by increasing the free float from 33% to 45% of the total number of shares in issue, or from BEF 71 billion to 115 billion in value terms.

The merger will also have an immediate favourable effect on the profits per share. On completion of the merger, which will increase the number of Tractebel shares in issue by 21%, the controlling shareholding of SOCIETE GENERALE de BELGIQUE will fall from 62.71% to 50.27% taking account of the operations mentioned in para. 3.3 below.
3.2 Share exchange ratio

On the basis of a comparison between the activities, strategies and financial situation of the two companies, using various criteria, the boards of TRACTEBEL and POWERFIN are proposing an exchange of three POWERFIN shares (coupon No. 9 and following attached) for one TRACTEBEL share (coupon No. 19 and following attached), i.e. after detachment of the coupons payable in 1997 for the financial year 1996.

The three-to-one ratio was based on a comparison of the two companies' respective assets and stock exchange prices and closely reflects the average of the two other comparative criteria, namely the dividend and the net consolidated profit per share.

In addition to having the appropriateness and reasonable nature of the exchange ratio examined by TRACTEBEL's and POWERFIN's own auditors (Deloitte & Touche, Ernst & Young and Meunier) as required by the Coordinated Laws on Commercial Companies (Companies Act) for this type of operation, the boards of the two companies also obtained the opinions of SBC WARBURG, a division of SWISS BANK CORPORATION, and of KREDIETBANK SECURITIES and PETERCAM SECURITIES in their capacity as investment banks. Their opinions confirm without qualification the fairness of the proposed exchange , both for TRACTEBEL shareholders and for POWERFIN shareholders, and from the financial point of view.
3.3 Timetable

The TRACTEBEL Board of Directors plans to call an Extraordinary General Meeting at the conclusion of the AGM on 28 May 1997 to discuss the merger. The Board will meet on 15 April to adopt the final terms of the detailed, written report, as required by art. 174/3 the Companies Act, and to approve the agenda for the AGM.

As part of this operation, the Board has decided that action should be taken to avoid creating or perpetuating a situation of auto-control within TRACTEBEL (i.e. with TRACTEBEL shares being held by TELFIN, or with POWERFIN shares held by group companies being converted into TRACTEBEL shares).
4. Company results and dividend
The net company profit for TRACTEBEL S.A. (non-consolidated) came to BEF 7,757 million in 1996, compared with BEF 7,305 million the previous year, an increase of BEF 452 million.
At the AGM on 28 May 1997, the Board will propose an increase in the net unit dividend for 1996 to BEF 385, up from BEF 370 for 1995.

In the case of dividend coupons accompanied by a strip giving entitlement to a lower rate of withholding tax, the dividend will come to BEF 436.33, compared with BEF 419.33 the year before. These dividends will be payable as of 11 June 1997 on presentation of No. 18 coupons. 5. Results and activities of business units Table omitted
5.1 Electricity in Belgium
The contribution by the Electricity in Belgium business unit to TRACTEBEL's share of profits has risen from BEF 8,732 million in 1995 to BEF 8,953 million in 1996, an increase of 2.5%.

However, the variation in the contribution is less than the +4.1% which it would have been under a direct comparison, due to some ELECTRABEL shares having been transferred out of the group. The fall in electricity consumption by industry in the fourth quarter of 1995 continued through most of 1996. However, the situation started to recover from September onwards, so that sales to industry were more or less at their normal level for the year overall. Sales of electricity for distribution rose by 3.9%. For the year as a whole, sales of electricity increased by 2% in 1996.

As of 1 April 1996, the various categories of consumers benefited from price reductions equivalent to a total of BEF 1.3 billion per year. On top of this effort on electricity rates, a second series of measures came into effect in 1997, representing a recurring annual amount of the order of 1,500 million for the electricity sector.

A large part of the gain in productivity was absorbed by a yet another increase in the level of taxation on ELECTRABEL, in the form of a special levy on electricity producers (an extra BEF 1.55 billion, or more than 25%).

A further development in 1996 was ELECTRABEL's acquisition of a stake of 3% in SCOTTISH POWER, the fourth-largest electricity producer in the UK. This investment of just over BEF 5 billion sealed an agreement for technology transfer between the two companies.
5.2 Gas in Belgium
The Gas in Belgium business unit contributed BEF 670 million in 1996 to TRACTEBEL's share of the consolidated profits, compared with 676 million in 1995, a slight drop of 0.9%.

Total sales grew by 11% for the second consecutive year, as a result of the expansion in sales to Public Distribution which rose by 16.6% following the cold weather in 1996. This favourable development was however largely offset by the tariff reduction of BEF 470 million recommended by the Electricity & Gas Board of Control.

Under the terms of an agreement made on 24 May 1994 with the Belgian government, 116,809 DISTRIGAS shares representing 16.62% of the company's share capital were floated on the Brussels stock exchange on 16 June 1996. The other planned transfers of shares to the municipalities took place in July 1996. These operations completed the redistribution of the DISTRIGAS shares, of which TRACTEBEL now controls more than 50%.

A considerable amount of work will have to be devoted to upgrading the DISTRIGAS transport and transit network in order to ensure transit through Belgium of the gas arriving via the Interconnector pipeline under the North Sea. Long-term contracts were signed with several foreign companies, and negotiations are under way with other companies for extra transit contracts, giving the green light for the investment programme aimed at expanding the network. The work will be carried out in 1997 and 1998. Commissioning is planned for October 1998, when Interconnector comes on stream.
5.3 Electricity and Gas International (EGI)

TRACTEBEL's share in the 1996 profits of the EGI business unit amounted to BEF 262 million, compared with BEF 290 million in 1995. This variation is due to the combined effect of two contrasting factors, namely:
1. The growth in profits of the operating companies, due mainly to:
- The increased contribution by CRSS in the USA, which was acquired in June 1995 and so only contributed to the results for six months of that year;
- the coming on-stream of the Al Manah power station in Oman;
2.The increased financial expenses and the costs of development investments.
Since the beginning of 1996, the group has acquired or developed ten new electricity or gas projects in Canada, Chile, the USA, Kazakhstan, Singapore and Thailand.

The combined electricity capacity of power stations in service, under construction or at an advanced stage of development in which EGI has a stake amounted to 9,576 MW on 31 December 1996. To this must be added the thermal capacity of 1,399 MW-equivalent for production of heat. In terms of the capacity actually owned by EGI, the figures are 4,021 MW and 752 MWeq respectively. At the same date, the annual volume of natural gas distributed amounted to 4.5 m3.
5.4 Communications

Net profits from the Communications business unit (TRACTEBEL's share) totalled BEF 193 million in 1996, compared with BEF 233 million in 1995, a reduction of 17.2%. This is mainly due to making provision for restructuring.

Pursuing its strategy of developing niches in the communications sector, TRACTEBEL concluded an agreement with the Dutch group Securicor Datatrak Europe in June 1996 setting up a communications network in Belgium for locating vehicles and exchanging brief messages. This will be carried out in Belgium by DATATRAK S.A, in which TRACTEBEL has a stake of 79%. Other projects are also being studied.
5.5 Technical Installations and Services to Communities (TISC)

The contribution by the TISC business unit to TRACTEBEL's share of the consolidated profit grew strongly from BEF 748 million in 1995 to BEF 1,136 million, an increase of 51.9%. This growth is partly due to the increase in TRACTEBEL's stake in GROUPE FABRICOM and in WATCO (the growth of the TISC sector, minority interests included, was 26.9% in 1996).

The Technical Installations sector managed to expand, despite the continuing poor state of the economy. AXIMA in particular contributed to the steady growth of the installations management sector. Solid Waste continued its growth in an expanding market. These favourable developments were achieved despite the deterioration in pylon construction sector and the restructuring operations necessary in the German subsidiaries of the Liquid Waste sector. The 1996 results were also favourably influenced by extraordinary income from sale of securities.

The contribution made by these elements to TRACTEBEL's consolidated profits was increased following raising of the group's stake in WATCO and GROUPE FABRICOM, and has also been influenced by the takeover of FIMEUSE (see below).
In the operational field, 1996 saw the continuation of GROUPE FABRICOM's strategy of growth by investment in Belgium and abroad, principally in Europe.
The dynamism of FABRICOM S.A. in technical installations activities outside Belgium was rewarded in 1996 with an Oscar for Exports in the category Services.

GROUPE FABRICOM also increased its participation in WATCO from 60% to 85.2%. The latter company heads a group of more than a hundred firms in the waste management sector in Belgium and neighbouring countries. An increase in its capital enabled WATCO to continue its policy of taking over existing companies and setting up new ones. The WATCO group in Belgium was also reorganised on a regional basis, reflecting the new structure of government and enabling it to accommodate the varying environmental regulations in the different regions.

GROUPE FABRICOM further reinforced the resources of its subsidiary EUROPEENE de SERVICES (EdS), tasked with developing Waste activities in countries other than Belgium's immediate neighbours. Thanks to these extra resources, EdS extended its operations in Poland and Canada.

In Autumn 1996, GROUPE FABRICOM pulled out of CONTINENTALE d'ENTREPRISES, which no longer fitted in with its strategic objectives. By the same token FABRICOM S.A. partially disengaged from its workshops in Bruges, transferring them to the company BEP EUROPE in which it now owns 40%.
GROUPE FABRICOM financed its expansion by two new share issues, one of BEF 2,500 million in June 1996 and the other of BEF 1,315 million in February 1997.

In May 1996, TRACTEBEL made an offer to the minority shareholders in FIMEUSE to exchange their shares for TRACTEBEL stock, at a rate of five FIMEUSE shares for eight TRACTEBEL . This raised TRACTEBEL's stake in FIMEUSE to 96.28%, and TRACTEBEL took FIMEUSE over at the end of December 1996.

The start of 1997 saw the acquisition by FABRICOM S.A. of ALVEY EUROPE in Willebroek and SANTENS ENGINEERING SERVICES, both specialising in automated systems for industrial logistics. EdS broke into the waste sector in the UK with the acquisition of a majority stake in LANCASHIRE WASTE SERVICES (LWS), one of the largest LAWDCs (Local Authority Waste Disposal Companies), when it was privatised.
5.6 Real Estate
TRACTEBEL's net share in the Real Estate sector doubled in 1996, from BEF 236 in 1995 to BEF 472 million.

This increase was mainly due to the recovery in the results of COMPAGNIE IMMOBILIERE DE BELGIQUE (CIB), which was back in the black in 1996, together with capital gains on the sale of certain buildings by TRACTEBEL ESPANA and the IMMOBILIERE TRACTEBEL division.

On the operational side, in 1996 IMMOBEL began construction on a number of sites which it controls either alone or in partnership, with a programme of developments representing a total floor area of 152,000 m2, of which IMMOBEL's share amounts to 120,000 m2.
The site development and property marketing activities also enjoyed significant growth in 1996.

COMPAGNIE IMMOBILIERE DE WALLONIE signed a contract in December 1996 for planned sale of a 14,500 m2 complex, including 9,260 m2 of office space on the site of the former Hopital des Anglais building in Liege.
Abroad, IMMOBEL is engaged in constructing a 20,000 m2 office building in the centre of Warsaw in partnership with the Buelens group.
Completion is scheduled for the end of 1997, and marketing of the project is proceeding satisfactorily.
5.7 Engineering

TRACTEBEL's net share increased from BEF 971 million in 1995 to BEF 1,008 million in 1996, a rise of 3.8%, despite the slow-down of investments in the Belgian electricity sector and manufacturing industry.
Projects completed in 1996 included:
- commissioning of the four last units of the Taweelha B seawater desalination plant in Abu Dhabi,
- commissioning of the Al Manah power station and electricity transmission line in Oman,
- turnkey delivery of vapour recovery systems for the Inchon LNG terminal in South Korea,
- the opening of the first section of High Speed Train railway line in Belgium,
- inauguration of a turnkey hospital project in Bratislava, Slovakia,
- the equipping of five LNG carrier ships (one in Indonesia, two in China, and two in the Netherlands).
Several new contracts were concluded abroad in 1996, for example in Algeria, the United Arab Emirates, Ethiopia, India, Russia, Shanghai, Taiwan and Vietnam.
On the investment side, TRACTEBEL ENGINEERING last year acquired 25% of the French company GEOSTOCK, the world leader in underground storage of hydrocarbons.
Overall, the volume of turnover earned outside Belgium in 1996 represented over a third of the consolidated figure for the Engineering business unit.
5.8 Parent company and other aspects of the results

The contribution to TRACTEBEL's share of the consolidated result by the parent company, financial subsidiaries and miscellaneous came to BEF 897 million, compared with BEF 441 million the previous year. This improvement is due to several factors, including the flotation and sale on the American NASDAQ market of part of TRACTEBEL's stake in SIPEX, a company specialising in analogue integrated circuits. A capital gain of the order of BEF 2 billion was generated by this operation.
A provision of BEF 1.6 million was set aside to cover the country risk associated with guarantees and investments by TRACTEBEL S.A. for projects abroad.

In terms of TRACTEBEL's share, the expense item "depreciation of goodwill"amounted to BEF 1,146 million in 1996 compared with only BEF 685 in 1995. This increase is a logical consequence of the TRACTEBEL group's investment strategy and of the accounting principles governing it, which are much more conservative than those applied by some foreign groups active in the same sector.
Finally, in 1996, the TRACTEBEL set up a European Social Dialogue Body in accordance with the EU Directive of 22 September 1994.
6. Other Board Decisions
The Board of Directors has accepted the resignations of Messrs. Frere, Dejounay and Scohier as directors.

The Board has appointed Mr. Antoon Dieusaert as a director, and appointed Messrs. De Keersmaeker and Dieusaert to the Restricted Committee. At the Extraordinary General Meeting on 28 May 1997, the Board intends to make a proposal reconstituting the Restricted Committee as a Strategic Committee. The AGM will be invited to confirm the appointment of Mr. Dieusaert.
Finally, the Board intends to propose renewing the clauses in the articles concerning purchase of the company's own shares and the authorised capital, at the AGM on 28 May 1997.
NOTES TO EDITORS
Tractebel

Tractebel is an international Belgian utility and industrial services group. The company has operations in electricity, gas, waste management, technical installations, engineering, communications and real estate.

Tractebel employs over 47.000 people and operates in more than 100 countries. Overall, Tractebel's installations represent 22,500 MW (*) of electricity generation capacity and the company manages transport installations carrying about 30 billion m3 (**) gas per year.

As a result of increasing liberalization of the world's electricity and gas markets, Tractebel has developed electricity and gas projects in 15 countries outside Belgium since the beginning of the nineties, (the USA, Argentina, Chile, Thailand, the Sultanate of Oman, Singapore, China, Kazakhstan, Hungary, Italy, Northern Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Canada, and India).

Tractebel now has a portfolio of 9,576 MW of electricity generation capacity, in operation or under construction, heat production installations equivalent to 1,399 MW and 4.5 billion m3 gas distribution outside Belgium.
Since 1995, the group has invested 21 billion BEF (650 million USD) in electricity and gas projects abroad.

In addition, the Belgian electricity company Electrabel, controlled by Tractebel, has formed a number of alliances with other European electricity companies, either through minority shareholdings (4.5% in Spain's Iberdrola and 3% in Scottish Power) or cooperation agreements (reserve capacity sharing agreement with the Dutch SEP, and capacity reservation in EDF power plants).

Waste management activities are increasingly important for Tractebel: over the past five years, solid waste management and water and sludge treatment operations have been developed in over 11 countries within the EC and central Europe.
Tractebel's main fields of activity are:
- electricity and gas operations in Europe, North and South America, the Middle East and South East Asia.
- waste management and the realisation and management of technical installations in Europe and Canada.
- engineering services worldwide.
- communications (cable TV and cellular phone networks) in Europe and the USA.
Tractebel controls two listed Belgian utilities, which operate under a regulated system:
- Electrabel: electricity generation, transmission and distribution of electricity and gas within Belgium.

- Distrigas: supply and transportation of natural gas within Belgium; gas transit (5% stake in the Interconnector-pipeline project between continental Europe and the UK; operation of the Zeebrugge LNG-terminal).
Tractebel also has interests in real estate, through Compagnie Immobiliere de Belgique (Immobel).

(*) By way of comparison, the German utility RWE has an electricity generation capacity of 26,000 MW, VEBA (Preussen Elektra) 14,800 MW, the US utility Southern Electric 30,700 MW (based on '95 figures provided by Morgan Stanley).
(**) 45 billion m3 after the commissioning of the Interconnector between Bacton (UK) and Zeebrugge (B)
